title: The Rust Programming Language
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The canonical guided tour. This curriculum follows its chapter order so every module has an authoritative long-form counterpart.

title: Rust by Example
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Runnable snippets for the same concepts. Use it when you want to see the shape of the code before reading the argument for it.

title: Rustlings
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Small compiler-error-driven fixes. Closest external analogue to this app's terminal work; good for extra repetitions.

title: The Rust Standard Library
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Primary API reference. Every collection, trait, and guarantee named in a lesson is specified here first.

title: The Rust Reference
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Language-level specification. Reach for it when you need the rule rather than an explanation of the rule.

title: The rustc Error Index
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: One page per E-code with a minimal reproduction and repair. The compiler-error nodes in the concept map link straight here.

title: The Cargo Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Manifest keys, profiles, workspaces, features, and publishing. The authority behind every cargo command this app runs.

title: The Edition Guide
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: What changed across 2015/2018/2021/2024. Read it before trusting an older blog post or Stack Overflow answer.

title: Comprehensive Rust
author: Google
blurb: A dense multi-day course with speaker notes, plus bare-metal, Android, and Chromium tracks the Book never covers.

title: The Rust Cookbook
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Task-shaped recipes using well-known crates. Useful once you know the language and need the ecosystem's default answer.

title: Rust Design Patterns
author: rust-unofficial
blurb: Idioms, patterns, and named anti-patterns. The vocabulary layer between 'it compiles' and 'a reviewer would accept it'.

title: Effective Rust
author: David Drysdale
blurb: Thirty-five specific pieces of advice on types, traits, dependencies, and tooling. Commercially published, so this app links to it and never reproduces it.

title: Rust API Guidelines
author: The Rust Library Team
blurb: The checklist library authors are held to: naming, interoperability, flexibility, future proofing.

title: The Rustonomicon
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The dark arts of unsafe Rust: aliasing, variance, drop order, and the invariants you now have to uphold by hand.

title: Learn Rust With Entirely Too Many Linked Lists
author: Aria Beingessner
blurb: The best available treatment of ownership under pressure. Work it after Chapter 15; it turns smart pointers into muscle memory.

title: Rust Atomics and Locks
author: Mara Bos
blurb: Free online edition covering memory ordering, building your own locks, and what the OS actually does underneath.

title: Asynchronous Programming in Rust
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Futures, executors, pinning, and cancellation from first principles rather than from one runtime's API surface.

title: Tokio Tutorial
author: The Tokio Contributors
blurb: The concrete counterpart to the async book: tasks, channels, select, shared state, and graceful shutdown in a real runtime.

title: The Little Book of Rust Macros
author: Veykril (community edition)
blurb: macro_rules! from fragment specifiers to hygiene, then the bridge into procedural macros.

title: The Rust Performance Book
author: Nicholas Nethercote
blurb: Profiling first, then measured wins: allocation, hashing, bounds checks, build configuration, and benchmarking discipline.

title: Rust Quiz
author: David Tolnay
blurb: Short programs with surprising output and a full explanation. Excellent calibration for how well you actually read Rust.

title: TheAlgorithms / Rust
author: TheAlgorithms community
blurb: Reference implementations for classic algorithms in idiomatic-ish Rust. Compare against your own after you have solved a pattern.

title: Exercism Rust Track
author: Exercism
blurb: Around a hundred graded exercises with published community solutions — the widest source of alternative idiom for a solved problem.

title: Learn Rust (rust-lang.org)
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The project's own index of official learning material. Start here to see what is canonical before trusting a third-party summary.

title: The rustc Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Compiler flags, lint levels, codegen options, and platform support. Read the lints chapter before you reach for #[allow].

title: The rustdoc Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: How doc comments, intra-doc links, and doctests work. Doctests are a second test suite most beginners never switch on.

title: Clippy Documentation
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Configuring and running Clippy, lint groups, and how to justify an allow. Pairs with the searchable lint list dataset below.

title: The Rust Style Guide
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The formatting rules rustfmt implements, with the reasoning. Useful when a formatting choice looks arbitrary.

title: rustfmt Configuration
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Every rustfmt.toml option with before/after examples, filterable by stable versus unstable.

title: The Unstable Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Nightly-only features and their tracking issues. Read it to understand where the language is going, not to build on it.

title: The Rust RFC Book
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: The accepted design documents behind every major feature. An RFC's 'Motivation' and 'Alternatives' sections explain why a rule is the way it is.

title: The FLS (Rust language specification)
author: The Rust Project (originally Ferrous Systems and AdaCore)
blurb: A rigorously structured specification of Rust, maintained by the Rust project since 2025. Numbered paragraphs make it the most citable language reference.

title: Unsafe Code Guidelines Reference
author: Rust Unsafe Code Guidelines Working Group
blurb: Layout, validity, and aliasing rules that unsafe code must uphold. Read after the Rustonomicon when you need the precise invariant.

title: Rust Compiler Development Guide
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: How rustc is built: HIR, MIR, type checking, and the borrow checker. The MIR borrow-check chapter shows what 'the borrow checker' literally computes.

title: Rust Forge
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Release trains, team structure, and contribution process. Where to go when you want to contribute to Rust itself.

title: rust-analyzer Manual
author: rust-analyzer contributors
blurb: Editor setup, assists, and inlay hints. Inlay type hints are the fastest way to see what inference decided.

title: Miri
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: An interpreter that detects undefined behaviour in tests. Run it on any crate that contains unsafe before you believe a safety comment.

title: Rust Playground
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Run snippets on stable, beta, or nightly and view MIR, LLVM IR, or assembly. Also runs Clippy and Miri on a snippet.

title: Compiler Explorer
author: Matt Godbolt and contributors
blurb: See the machine code rustc emits side by side with source. It turns 'zero-cost abstraction' from a slogan into something you can check.

title: The Rust Book: Experimental Edition (Brown University)
author: Will Crichton, Gavin Gray, Shriram Krishnamurthi (Cognitive Engineering Lab)
blurb: The official Book with embedded quizzes, a redesigned ownership chapter, and 'Ownership Inventory' scenarios. Its quiz data drove published research on how people learn Rust.

title: Rust By Practice
author: sunface and contributors
blurb: Fill-in and fix-the-bug exercises organised by the same topics as the Book, with published solutions. Good for a second round after each chapter.

title: 100 Exercises to Learn Rust
author: Luca Palmieri (Mainmatter)
blurb: A test-driven course built around one ticketing domain. The app already embeds this pack as its Mainmatter practice track; the upstream site has the prose.

title: Easy Rust
author: Dave MacLeod
blurb: The whole language in simple English with short examples. A good second explanation when the Book's phrasing does not land.

title: Tour of Rust
author: Richard Anaya and contributors
blurb: Bite-sized pages each with a runnable example, translated into many languages. Fast syntax orientation before the deeper chapters.

title: A Gentle Introduction to Rust
author: Steve Donovan
blurb: A pragmatic tour aimed at programmers from other languages, with a candid 'pain points' chapter.

title: Rust for C++ Programmers
author: Nick Cameron
blurb: Maps unique_ptr, shared_ptr, and references onto Box, Rc, and borrows. Read it if you already think in C++ ownership terms.

title: Rust Language Cheat Sheet
author: Ralf Biedert
license: Code snippets CC0-1.0; prose free to read
blurb: Dense one-page reference with memory-layout diagrams for String, Vec, Box, and Rc. Keep it open while doing exercises.

title: Command Line Applications in Rust
author: Rust CLI Working Group
blurb: A 15-minute CLI tutorial followed by chapters on argument parsing, errors, output, and testing binaries. A natural first real project after chapter 11.

title: The Embedded Rust Book
author: Rust Embedded Working Group
license: Prose CC-BY-SA-4.0; code MIT OR Apache-2.0
blurb: no_std, peripherals as owned singletons, and interrupts. Shows ownership modelling hardware, not just memory.

title: Discovery (micro:bit v2)
author: Rust Embedded Working Group
license: Prose CC-BY-4.0; code MIT OR Apache-2.0
blurb: A beginner embedded course on an inexpensive micro:bit board, from blinking an LED to serial communication.

title: The Embedonomicon
author: Rust Embedded Working Group
license: Prose CC-BY-SA-4.0; code MIT OR Apache-2.0
blurb: Build a no_std program from nothing: linker scripts, the reset handler, and memory layout.

title: Writing an OS in Rust
author: Philipp Oppermann
license: Prose CC-BY-NC-4.0; code MIT OR Apache-2.0
blurb: A step-by-step x86_64 kernel: VGA output, interrupts, paging, heap allocation, and async tasks. The best long project for unsafe and no_std.

title: Rust and WebAssembly
author: Rust and WebAssembly Working Group (archived)
blurb: Game of Life compiled to WebAssembly, with profiling and size optimisation. The organisation is archived, but the model of the JS/Wasm boundary still holds.

title: Serde
author: Erick Tryzelaar, David Tolnay
blurb: How the de facto serialization framework uses traits and derive macros. The data-model page is a masterclass in trait design.

title: Criterion.rs User Guide
author: Brook Heisler and contributors
blurb: Statistics-driven benchmarking. Pair it with the Performance Book so optimisations are measured rather than guessed.

title: Rust Fuzz Book
author: rust-fuzz contributors
blurb: cargo-fuzz and afl.rs from first target to structure-aware fuzzing. The next step after unit and property tests.

title: mini-redis
author: Tokio contributors
blurb: An intentionally readable Redis server written to teach Tokio. Read it alongside the Tokio tutorial.

title: Procedural Macros Workshop
author: David Tolnay
blurb: Five test-driven projects that build real derive, attribute, and function-like macros. The practical sequel to the Little Book of Rust Macros.

title: Rust Algorithm Club
author: Weihang Lo and contributors
blurb: Classic algorithms and data structures explained with Rust implementations. Useful beside the interview-practice track.

title: Take your first steps with Rust (Microsoft Learn)
author: Microsoft
blurb: A free guided learning path with sandboxed exercises. Another voice for the chapter 1–11 material.

title: ripgrep
author: Andrew Gallant
blurb: A production command-line tool with exemplary error handling, crate boundaries, and comments. The standard recommendation for 'show me good Rust'.

title: uutils coreutils
author: uutils contributors
blurb: Rust rewrites of ls, cat, wc, and friends. Each utility is small enough to read in one sitting and has a known specification.

title: The standard library source
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Every std doc page has a 'Source' link. Reading Vec, Option, and RefCell's implementations shows small audited unsafe wrapped in safe APIs.

title: axum examples
author: Tokio contributors
blurb: Dozens of small, focused web-service examples (the framework this app's own service uses).

title: rustc UI test suite
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Thousands of small programs paired with the exact diagnostics rustc must print. The largest corpus of 'predict the compiler error' drills in existence.

title: rustc error-code explanations (source)
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: One Markdown file per E-code with an erroneous example and a fix: the machine-readable source behind the Error Index.

title: Clippy lint list
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Over 800 lints, each with 'what it does', 'why is this bad', and a before/after example. Browse one category a week as an idiom curriculum.

title: RustSec Advisory Database
author: Rust Secure Code Working Group
blurb: Every published vulnerability in a crates.io crate. Reading the unsafe-related advisories is a catalogue of real soundness bugs.

title: crates.io database dump
author: crates.io team
license: Access policy CC-BY-4.0; data licences documented in the dump
blurb: A daily CSV export of crate, version, and dependency metadata. A realistic dataset for your own parsing, graph, and analytics projects.

title: Rust Quiz question sources
author: David Tolnay
blurb: The source of each Rust Quiz puzzle with its explanation, ready for self-study offline.

title: Awesome Rust
author: rust-unofficial contributors
blurb: The long curated list of Rust applications, libraries, and tools. Use it to find prior art before writing something.

title: Awesome Embedded Rust
author: Rust Embedded Working Group
blurb: HALs, board-support crates, drivers, and RTOS options, organised by chip family.

title: docs.rs
author: docs.rs team
blurb: API documentation for every published crate version. Read a crate's docs before adding it as a dependency.

title: This Week in Rust
author: This Week in Rust editors
blurb: The weekly digest of articles, releases, and calls for participation. Skim the 'Crate of the Week' as a gentle ecosystem tour.

title: The Rust Blog
author: The Rust Project Developers
blurb: Release announcements every six weeks explain each newly stabilised feature with an example.

title: Rust Users Forum
author: Rust community
blurb: The official place to ask for help. Searching it for your exact error message usually finds a worked explanation.

title: Crust of Rust (video series)
author: Jon Gjengset
blurb: Long-form live coding that builds std types from scratch: iterators, smart pointers, channels, atomics. Watch after the matching chapter here.

title: Rust conference talks
author: The Rust Foundation and conference organisers
blurb: RustConf and other conference talks. Good for how teams use Rust in production and why features were designed as they were.

title: A Grounded Conceptual Model for Ownership Types in Rust
author: Will Crichton, Gavin Gray, Shriram Krishnamurthi (OOPSLA 2023)
blurb: The research behind the Brown edition's permissions model of borrowing (read/write/own). If ownership still feels like magic, this model is the fix.

title: Profiling Programming Language Learning
author: Will Crichton, Shriram Krishnamurthi (OOPSLA 2024)
blurb: What 1.1 million quiz answers revealed about where Rust learners struggle, and which interventions helped. It shaped this app's question design.

title: RustBelt: Securing the Foundations of Rust
author: Ralf Jung, Jacques-Henri Jourdan, Robbert Krebbers, Derek Dreyer (POPL 2018)
blurb: A machine-checked proof that safe Rust plus correctly encapsulated unsafe code is memory safe. The theory behind 'wrap unsafe in a safe API'.
